message.content: [Synthetic demo] Our LRU cache sometimes evicts entries that are still pinned. `npm test -- cache` fails intermittently. Please find and fix the race in src/cache/evict.ts.

content.text: Let me look at the eviction path first to see how pinned entries are tracked.
The pin check happens before the sort, but eviction runs async — an entry can be pinned between the check and the actual delete. Let me read the full eviction loop.
Found it: `flushToDisk` awaits between the refCount check (line 32) and the delete (line 36). If `pin()` runs during the flush, we delete a pinned entry. Fix: re-check refCount after the await.
The file src/cache/evict.ts has been updated.
Running the cache test suite to confirm.

FAIL test/cache.test.ts
  ✓ evicts least-recently-used first (12 ms)
  ✕ never evicts a pinned entry (34 ms)

  ● never evicts a pinned entry
    expected cache.get('pinned-key') to be defined

Tests: 1 failed, 1 passed
Still failing — the test pins via a WeakRef wrapper, so `entry.refCount` is stale in the loop. I need to re-read the entry from the map instead of trusting the captured reference.

input.old_string:
// Re-check after the await: the entry may have been pinned mid-flush.
      if (entry.refCount > 0) continue;

content.text: The file src/cache/evict.ts has been updated.

PASS test/cache.test.ts
  ✓ evicts least-recently-used first (11 ms)
  ✓ never evicts a pinned entry (29 ms)

Tests: 2 passed, 2 total

Fixed. The race was a TOCTOU between the pin check and the delete across the `flushToDisk` await:

- `evictBatch` now re-reads the **live** entry from the map after the await and skips it when `refCount > 0` (or when it was replaced).
- Both cache tests pass.

The first attempt (re-checking the captured reference) wasn't enough because the test pins through a fresh lookup — a good reminder that after any suspension point you must re-validate against the source of truth, not a captured snapshot.
